parts: if you want to go the discrete route, you'll have to do something like cut() on z (see below)  and also fiddle with scale_fill_manual. this is nearly the same as what brandon did with _gradientn

conc20<-melt(mat_conc20)

conc20$z=cut(conc20$z,6,include.lowest=TRUE)
conc20_cont <- ggplot(conc20, aes(x, y, z = z))
conc20_cont + geom_tile(aes(fill=z)) + scale_fill_manual(values=c("blue","lightblue","green","yellow","orange","red"))

messages.subject: Re: Tired of filled.contour, want to use geom_tile
parts:
what brandon showed was for continuous variables, ie using scale_gradientn(). i only suggested discretizing since you originally used scale_manual(). look at scale_gradientn() for more details on including pre-defined colour pallettes, e.g.

conc20_cont + geom_tile(aes(fill=z)) + scale_fill_gradientn(colour=(rainbow(7)[7:1]))

What Brandon did (based on your original colours) matched your previous graph much better.

The rainbow graph was definitely worse. I think the blending is probably more of a function of geom_tile vs contour rather than the color scale. Could be wrong though, as I don't have much experience with contours. 

B

On Fri, Jan 14, 2011 at 17:25, James McCreight <mccr...@colorado.edu> wrote:
what brandon showed was for continuous variables, ie using scale_gradientn(). i only suggested discretizing since you originally used scale_manual(). look at scale_gradientn() for more details on including pre-defined colour pallettes, e.g.

conc20_cont + geom_tile(aes(fill=z)) + scale_fill_gradientn(colour=(rainbow(7)[7:1]))

What Brandon did (based on your original colours) matched your previous graph much better.
